audit_summary: Accepted 13 facts as directly supported by the reopened files. Rejected F3 because its exclusivity claim conflicts with the separate package-subtree skipping behavior in the same function.

facts.statement: The `recursive` option enables discovery of Python modules and packages in a filesystem subtree and defaults to false.
When recursive mode is enabled, `check` replaces the original arguments with the paths yielded by `_discover_files`.
For walked directories without `__init__.py`, `_discover_files` yields every `.py` file by joining the walked root and filename; it does not apply ignore predicates to each file at this point.
The shared ignore predicate matches `ignore` and `ignore-patterns` against the basename, but matches `ignore-paths` against the complete path string passed to it.
After recursive discovery, file expansion invokes `expand_modules` with the configured ignore names, ignore patterns, and the linter's cached ignore-path patterns.
`expand_modules` applies the complete ignore predicate to every input path before resolving or adding it, so recursively yielded files have a second opportunity to be excluded.
The `ignore-paths` option is documented as matching regex patterns against paths in either Posix or Windows format.

Each configured ignore-path expression is compiled as an alternation of a Windows-normalized representation and a Posix-normalized representation; no third representation for a path containing mixed `/` and `\` separators is generated.

TOML configuration supports nested sections such as `[tool.pylint.MASTER]`: dictionary entries are converted into command-line-style option/value arguments, so an `ignore-paths` value under that section is parsed as a linter option.
Configuration-file options are parsed before command-line options, and command-line options can override them.

The end-to-end recursive ignore-path test supplies `--ignore-paths=.*ignored.*` and `--ignore-paths=.*failing.*`; these patterns are unanchored with respect to the beginning and end of the reported relative path form.

The lower-level parametrized recursive-ignore test covers ignore-path values `.*directory/ignored.*` and `.*ignored.*/failing.*`, then constructs the lint target using the platform-aware `join` helper.
The ignore-path normalization unit test verifies fully Posix and fully Windows path strings, but does not include a mixed-separator path string.

scope_summary: Base commit 3c5eca2ded3dd2b59ebaf23eb289453b5d2930f0 defines recursive discovery and ignore-path filtering, but recursive file paths can retain mixed separators when the supplied directory ends with the non-native separator; configured ignore-path regexes are normalized only into all-Windows and all-Posix alternatives. Existing recursive ignore-path tests use broad unanchored patterns and repository-generated paths, so they do not cover the reported anchored relative-path case.
unknowns: The supplied repository cannot directly establish the exact runtime path string produced on the reporter's Windows/Python environment; it only establishes the path construction and regex-normalization behavior that can produce a mismatch.
The repository contains no test using the reported anchored pattern `^src/gen/.*$` together with a recursive target spelled `src/` on Windows.
